name: spa_keystore_change_key_sync
prose: Sync-task function that changes a dataset's wrapping key (dsl_crypt.c:1540-1633, void). It holds the dataset (VERIFY0) and asserts it is not a snapshot. For DCP_CMD_NEW_KEY it takes the wrapping key from the params and sets its ddobj; for DCP_CMD_FORCE_NEW_KEY it uses keylocation 'prompt' and has no wrapping key (wkey stays NULL). For these two commands it sets the keylocation property locally only if keylocation is non-NULL (for NEW_KEY that is only when cp_keylocation was supplied; for FORCE_NEW_KEY it is always set to 'prompt'), and takes the current encryption root as the old root and the dataset's own dir as the new root. For the inherit commands (DCP_CMD_INHERIT holds the parent's wrapping key in wkey; FORCE_INHERIT does not) it clears the keylocation property (source NONE), takes the dataset's dir as old root and the parent's encryption root as new root. It then takes sk_wkeys_lock as writer, calls spa_keystore_change_key_sync_impl(old root, dd_object, new root, wkey, B_FALSE, tx), removes and frees any cached wrapping key for this dataset's ddobj (asserting its refcount is 0), and inserts the new key into the keystore AVL tree only for DCP_CMD_NEW_KEY (FORCE_NEW_KEY and the two inherit commands insert nothing); for DCP_CMD_INHERIT it releases the parent key hold taken above. It releases the lock and the dataset hold. The function returns void.
note: Reviewers: original right (FORCE_NEW_KEY inserts no key, 1623-1628); round 15 right (for NEW_KEY the keylocation is set only when cp_keylocation is non-NULL, 1572). Callee not read.

name: spa_do_crypt_abd
prose: Encrypts or decrypts one block held in abds (dsl_crypt.c:2808-2896; the packet name zio_do_crypt does not exist, the slice cut the head). It asserts the encryption feature is active and looks up the key for zb->zb_objset in the keystore; if that fails it returns EACCES at once, before touching any buffer or the salt/iv/mac outputs. It borrows the plain and cipher buffers (the input one by copy). When encrypting a non-intent-log, non-dedup block it fills the salt (zio_crypt_key_get_salt) and a random IV; when encrypting a dedup block it derives the IV and salt from an HMAC of the plaintext; a failure of either goes to error. For decryption (and for encrypting ZIL blocks, whose salt/iv were generated at allocation) it uses the caller-provided salt and iv. It then calls zio_do_crypt_data with the key, mac and no_crypt; and, if fault injection is enabled, for a successful decryption of a non-DNODE object it may replace the result with zio_handle_decrypt_injection(..., ECKSUM). A non-zero result goes to error; on success it returns the buffers (the output buffer by copy-back), releases the key hold with spa_keystore_dsl_key_rele and returns 0. At error, when encrypting it zeroes the salt, iv and mac outputs, returns the buffers the same way, releases the key hold and returns the error value; when decrypting it returns the buffers and releases the key hold. Return value: 0, EACCES, or the callee's or injected error.
note: Real function is spa_do_crypt_abd; old drop was only because the name was not in the slice. Callee bodies not read.

name: dsl_scan_check_suspend
prose: Decides whether the scan should suspend now (dsl_scan.c:1643-1720, returns boolean_t). In order: returns B_FALSE if zb is non-NULL and zb_object (as signed) is negative, even if scn_suspending is already set; returns B_TRUE if scn_suspending is already set (without changing the bookmark); returns B_FALSE if the saved scn_bookmark is not zero (resuming); returns B_FALSE if zb is non-NULL and its level is neither 0 nor ZB_ROOT_LEVEL. Otherwise it computes scan time, sync time and the dirty-data threshold, and if any suspend condition holds (scan time over the minimum and (dirty data at or above the threshold, or a txg sync is waiting, or the sync time reached zfs_txg_timeout), or the spa is shutting down, or strict memory limiting wants a clear, or the DDT walk is not ready) it records where to resume: for a root-level zb it sets the bookmark to (objset, 0, 0, 0), for another non-NULL zb it copies *zb into scn_bookmark, and for a NULL zb (DDT suspend) it leaves scn_bookmark unchanged (it only logs the DDT bookmark in debug builds); in all three cases it then sets scn_suspending = B_TRUE and returns B_TRUE. If no suspend condition holds it returns B_FALSE.
note: Reviewers: original right (already-suspending returns true without setting a bookmark; the DDT suspend sets none, 1698-1716); round 15 right (the negative-object check comes first and returns B_FALSE even when scn_suspending is set, 1646-1650).

name: dsl_scan_sync
prose: Per-txg scan sync entry point (dsl_scan.c:4354-4669, void). Beginning: if spa_resilver_deferred it activates the RESILVER_DEFER feature if needed and computes restart_early (defer disabled, or fewer blocks issued than the configured percent of the to-examine count). It returns at once if spa_sync_pass > 1. If the scan is restarting (dsl_scan_restarting) or restart_early is set it ends the current scan with dsl_scan_done(scn, B_FALSE, tx) and starts a new scrub, or resilver when a vdev needs one, with dsl_scan_setup_sync (this dirties scan state) and then continues. It then returns if the pool is shutting down, if the sync txg is before spa_first_txg + zfs_import_defer_txgs, or if async destroys are not stalled and no scan is active. Past those, it resets the per-txg statistics counters, clears scn_suspending, records scn_sync_start_time and sets spa->spa_scrub_active = B_TRUE (so these are done before the following early returns). It runs dsl_process_async_destroys and returns if that gave an error; returns if no scan is running or the scrub is paused; and, if zfs_scan_suspend_progress is set, it waits (in one-second delays) until the minimum time passes, a txg sync is waiting or the pool shuts down, and returns. Otherwise it optionally reports statistics every zfs_scan_report_txgs, sets the checkpoint state, then, when the scan is not clearing and not done, it traverses (the main scan work branch: DDT scan then dsl_scan_visit with prefetch tasks and bookkeeping, reporting stats), else for a sorted scan with queues pending it issues the queued I/O, else when scn_done_txg is reached it finishes the scan. The remaining work-branch details (lines 4549-4669) were only skimmed for structure.
note: Reviewers: original right (the deferred restart calls dsl_scan_done/dsl_scan_setup_sync; early returns for async-destroy error, paused scrub and suspend-progress); round 15 right (stats reset and spa_scrub_active are set before those early returns, 4436-4450). Partly read: lines 4501-4669 not read in detail.

name: metaslab_activate
prose: Activates a metaslab for an allocator (metaslab.c:3591-3665). The caller must hold ms_lock (ASSERT). An already-active metaslab is accepted: if ms_weight has an active bit set it asserts the metaslab is loaded and returns 0 immediately, without checking the allocator or activation weight. Otherwise it calls metaslab_load; on error it resorts the metaslab in its group with weight 0 and returns that error (what state metaslab_load leaves the metaslab in on failure was not read). If, after loading (the lock may have been dropped during load), the metaslab became active, it returns EBUSY if ms_allocator differs from allocator or if the active weight bits do not include activation_weight, else (after an EQUIV assertion about the primary flag) returns 0. If ms_weight is 0 it asserts the allocatable range tree is empty and returns ENOSPC. Otherwise it calls metaslab_activate_allocator(group, msp, allocator, activation_weight) and returns its error if non-zero, else asserts the metaslab is loaded and active and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original right (an already-active metaslab returns 0 and the allocator may differ, 3606-3608); round 15 right that a load failure does not leave the metaslab known to be loaded (it only resorts the group and returns the error, 3611-3614). metaslab_load and metaslab_activate_allocator not read.

name: metaslab_should_condense
prose: Static boolean_t (metaslab.c:3836-3862) with one parameter, msp. It asserts ms_lock held, the metaslab loaded, a space map present and sync pass 1. It returns B_TRUE at once if the allocatable range tree has no segments or ms_condense_wanted is set. Otherwise it computes record_size = MAX(sm_blksz, vdev_blocksize), where vdev_blocksize is a local variable set to 1ULL << vd->vdev_ashift (it is not a parameter of this function), object_size = space_map_length(sm) and optimal_size = space_map_estimate_optimal_size(sm, ms_allocatable, SM_NO_VDEVID), and returns B_TRUE only if object_size >= optimal_size * zfs_condense_pct / 100 AND object_size > zfs_metaslab_condense_block_threshold * record_size; otherwise B_FALSE. No state is modified.
note: Reviewer round 15 WRONG for this source: vdev_blocksize is a local initialised from vdev_ashift (metaslab.c:3840), there is no vdev_blocksize argument. Callees not read.

name: spa_wait_tag
prose: Thin wrapper (spa.c:11577-11581) that returns spa_wait_common(pool, activity, B_TRUE, tag, waited). The slice mostly shows spa_wait_common (spa.c:11510-11570), whose behaviour is: with use_tag it returns EINVAL unless the activity is ZPOOL_WAIT_INITIALIZE or ZPOOL_WAIT_TRIM, and returns EINVAL for an activity outside the valid range, before touching the pool; it opens the pool (returning spa_open's error), takes spa_activities_lock, increments spa_waiters and closes the pool handle. It sets *waited = B_FALSE and loops: it calls spa_activity_in_progress; it leaves the loop if that returned an error, if the activity (or, with a tag, that tag) is not in progress (this includes a tag that is absent), or if spa_waiters_cancel is set (so it can return 0 without the activity having finished); otherwise it sets *waited = B_TRUE and waits on spa_activities_cv, returning EINTR if the wait was interrupted. It then decrements spa_waiters, signals spa_waiters_cv, drops the lock and returns error (0 when it left because of no activity in progress or because of the cancel flag, an errno otherwise). So the tag need not be in progress and *waited stays false when no wait happened.
note: Slice shows the helper; the named function is the wrapper. Reviewers: original right (a tag need not be in progress; returns 0 with *waited false when absent); round 15 right (spa_waiters_cancel can end the wait with 0 without the activity completing, spa.c:11553). spa_activity_in_progress not read.

name: spa_ld_select_uberblock
prose: Selects the uberblock to use during pool load (spa.c:4720-4884, returns int). Early return: if the current uberblock has a checkpoint txg and the pool is being imported read-only from its checkpoint it calls spa_ld_select_uberblock_done and returns 0 immediately, skipping the label search and the feature recording. Otherwise it loads the best uberblock and label with vdev_uberblock_load and returns spa_vdev_err(VDEV_AUX_CORRUPT_DATA, ENXIO) if no valid uberblock (txg 0) was found (freeing the label). It logs the chosen txg (and the raidz reflow info if set) and runs the multihost activity check when required: a failure maps through spa_ld_activity_result, frees the label and returns that error; when not required it records MMP result ESRCH. It returns spa_vdev_err(VDEV_AUX_VERSION_NEWER, ENOTSUP) if the on-disk version is unsupported (label freed); for versions with feature flags it requires the label to exist and have the features-for-read nvlist (otherwise ENXIO via spa_vdev_err), and stores a duplicate of that list in spa_label_features. It frees the label, then returns spa_vdev_err(VDEV_AUX_UNSUP_FEAT, ENOTSUP) with the unsupported feature list recorded in spa_load_info if any feature in the label is unsupported. If not assembling and a config split is in progress, it takes the config lock as writer, calls spa_try_repair (which has no return value here) and clears spa_config_splitting. Finally it calls spa_ld_select_uberblock_done and returns 0.
note: Reviewers: original right (the read-only checkpoint path returns before the label search, 4743-4747); round 15 WRONG: spa_try_repair is called as a statement and no error is returned from the config-splitting repair (4870-4876). Callees not read.

name: spa_export_common
prose: Common export/destroy path (spa.c:7652-7845, returns int). It sets *oldconfig = NULL if given. Without the namespace lock held by the caller (it takes spa_namespace_lock itself, so the caller must not hold it) it returns, before any state change or async suspend: EROFS if the global mode is not writable, ENOENT if the pool does not exist, ZFS_ERR_EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS if another export of the pool is running. It then marks spa_is_exporting, takes a reference, drops the namespace lock, suspends async tasks, removes zvol minors, retakes the lock and records the export thread. If the pool is UNINITIALIZED it jumps to export_spa. Otherwise it waits for a sync when sync is on; goes to fail with EBUSY if the pool is still referenced or has injection references; drops the namespace lock; if sync is on: with !force and EXPORTED it goes to fail with EXDEV if an active shared spare exists (after retaking the namespace lock); otherwise stops initialize, trim, autotrim, rebuild and the L2ARC rebuild, unless hardforce (or new state UNINITIALIZED) it marks the new state and dirties the vdev config, flushes the sync-time logger and log space maps when appropriate and, unless hardforce, sets spa_final_txg. At export_spa it runs spa_export_os, sends the destroy or export event, unloads and deactivates the pool unless uninitialised, copies the config into *oldconfig when asked and present, applies the export-delay injection, retakes the namespace lock and, for new states other than UNINITIALIZED, writes the cache file (skipped when hardforce) and calls spa_remove; for UNINITIALIZED it only clears spa_is_exporting and spa_export_thread. It broadcasts the namespace condition, drops the lock and returns 0. The fail label clears spa_is_exporting and the export thread, resumes async tasks, broadcasts and returns the error; the early EROFS, ENOENT and EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS returns do none of that (they have not suspended async work or set the flags).
note: Reviewers: original right (the function takes spa_namespace_lock itself and returns ENOENT for a missing pool); round 15 right (hardforce skips the cache file write, 7814-7815, and the early EROFS/ENOENT/IN_PROGRESS returns do not resume async or clear flags). Callees not read.

name: vdev_offline_locked
prose: Offlines a leaf vdev (vdev.c:4551-4659, returns int, every return goes through spa_vdev_state_exit). It enters vdev state with SCL_ALLOC and looks the vdev up by guid: ENODEV if not found, ENOTSUP if it is not a leaf or is a dRAID spare. If the vdev is not already offline: for a non-log, non-aux vdev whose DTL is required it returns EBUSY; for a log (slog) vdev with a metaslab group it passivates the group, leaves vdev state, calls spa_reset_logs, sets the error to ZFS_ERR_CHECKPOINT_EXISTS if the log top vdev has a non-empty checkpoint space map, re-enters vdev state and, if there was an error or the config generation changed, re-activates the group and either returns that error (including an error from spa_reset_logs or ZFS_ERR_CHECKPOINT_EXISTS) or, when only the generation changed, retries from the top. It then sets vdev_offline and reopens the top vdev; for a non-log, non-aux vdev if the top vdev is then dead it clears vdev_offline, reopens and returns EBUSY. On the success path for a slog it re-activates the metaslab group (vdev.c:4652-4653), so the group is not left passivated. Finally, in all non-error cases it sets vdev_tmpoffline from ZFS_OFFLINE_TEMPORARY and returns the result of spa_vdev_state_exit(spa, vd, 0), which is 0 on success.
note: Reviewers: original right (ZFS_ERR_CHECKPOINT_EXISTS and spa_reset_logs error returns for log devices); round 15 WRONG: after offlining a slog the code calls metaslab_group_activate(mg) (vdev.c:4652-4653). Callees not read.

name: vdev_prop_get
prose: Fills outnvl with vdev properties (vdev.c:6308-6799; the slice cut the head). It asserts vd and the meta objset are set, then returns EINVAL if innvl lacks ZPOOL_VDEV_PROPS_GET_VDEV (the vdev guid), and EINVAL if the vdev's property object id cannot be found. The ZPOOL_VDEV_PROPS_GET_PROPS list in innvl is optional: its absence is not an error. With spa_props_lock held it handles two modes. If a property list was given, it processes each requested name: for each property that has a value for this vdev it adds an entry to outnvl and continues; some properties are only added when applicable and otherwise skipped without an error, e.g. name when no string, path, devid, physpath, enclosure path and fru when NULL, parent when there is no parent, children when there are none, RAIDZ_EXPANDING only for raidz vdevs, SIT_OUT only for leaf vdevs with the required conditions, TRIM_SUPPORT only for leaf vdevs, ALLOCATING/AUTOSIT conditional parts, and the stored user/comment properties are read from the ZAP (a stored integer of size 8 gives EINVAL, a missing one an error); an unknown property name sets err = ENOENT; the first non-zero err stops the loop. Without a list it iterates the whole property ZAP of the vdev, adding string-valued and integer-valued stored properties (user properties as local source). It then releases spa_props_lock and returns err if it is non-zero and not ENOENT, else 0, so an ENOENT result (unknown or missing property) is not reported as an error. Properties that are not present for the vdev are skipped, not added with a default.
note: Slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 right (some requested properties are skipped, e.g. RAIDZ_EXPANDING on non-raidz, SIT_OUT/TRIM_SUPPORT on ineligible vdevs); round 17 (EINVAL for a missing property list) is not supported: the PROPS lookup result is ignored (6330-6331). Partly read: the individual numeric property cases at lines 6359-6590 were skimmed for their conditions, not read value by value.

name: vdev_inuse
prose: Decides whether a device label shows the device is in use (vdev_label.c:891-1016, returns boolean_t). It first sets *spare_guid and *l2cache_guid to 0 if those pointers are non-NULL. It returns B_FALSE if the label cannot be read, if the pool state or device guid is missing, or, for non-spare non-l2cache labels, if the pool guid or pool txg is missing. For a non-spare, non-l2cache label it returns B_FALSE if neither the pool guid pair nor a spare nor an l2cache with that device guid is known, and returns B_TRUE if txg == 0 and the label's create txg equals crtxg (this B_TRUE case requires that the label state is not spare or l2cache). If the device guid is a known spare (spa_spare_exists or spa_has_spare) it sets *spare_guid = device_guid (even if the function then returns B_FALSE) and, depending on reason, returns B_TRUE for CREATE, (!spa_has_spare || spare_pool != 0) for REPLACE, spa_has_spare for SPARE, or falls through for other reasons. Likewise for a known l2cache device it sets *l2cache_guid and returns B_TRUE for CREATE, !spa_has_l2cache for REPLACE, spa_has_l2cache for L2CACHE, or falls through. Finally, for non-spare non-l2cache labels whose pool is found by guid and open read-only, the state is treated as ACTIVE; it returns state == POOL_STATE_ACTIVE. So *spare_guid / *l2cache_guid can be non-zero even when the return is B_FALSE.
note: Reviewers: original right (the guid outputs are set before the reason switch, so they can be non-zero with a false result, 959-962 and 982-985); round 15 right (the txg == 0 shortcut also requires a non-spare, non-l2cache state, 950-951).

name: MUL_x2_DEFINE(x)
prose: Macro (vdev_raidz_math_avx512f.c:249-251) that generates 'static void mul_x2_<x>(void)' for x = 0..35 (invoked at lines 254-262): each function expands _MUL_PARAM(x, 21, 22 as input, 23, 24 as accumulator), emitting inline AVX-512 instructions that multiply the data held in the register pair zmm21, zmm22 (two 512-bit vectors) by the constant x in GF(2^8) and leave the product in the pair zmm23, zmm24. The expansion is decided at compile time from x: bit 0 of x selects COPY(in, acc) versus ZERO(acc) for the accumulator; each further multiplication by 2 (MUL2 on the input pair) is performed only if x has a higher bit set, and each XOR(in, acc) is done if the corresponding bit of x is set. So for x = 0 only the accumulator is zeroed (input untouched), and for x = 1 the input is copied to the accumulator and the input registers are not modified; for x >= 2 the input pair zmm21/zmm22 is overwritten by the successive doublings (MUL2 also uses scratch registers, including zmm25 and zmm26, and the constants set up by MUL2_SETUP, which the caller must have prepared). The generated function takes no arguments, has no return value and acts only on the zmm registers; it does not access memory.
note: Macro-generated; the name is the definition head, the real functions are mul_x2_0 ... mul_x2_35. Reviewers: round 15 right (x = 0 and 1 do not clobber the input, and the vectors are two registers); round 17 right (for x = 0 or 1 the scratch registers are not clobbered, because MUL2 is never emitted, lines 227-246). The exact scratch register list of MUL2 (lines 150-205) was only partly read.

name: spa_vdev_noalloc
prose: Marks a top-level vdev as no-allocate (vdev_removal.c:306-336, returns int). It asserts the namespace lock is not held on entry and the pool is writeable, then calls spa_vdev_enter(spa) (which takes the namespace lock and returns a txg). It looks the vdev up by guid: error ENOENT if not found; ZFS_ERR_VDEV_NOTSUP if the vdev has no metaslab group; if the vdev is not already noalloc, error = vdev_passivate(vd, &txg) (which may return an error such as EINVAL, not read; vdev_noalloc may already have been set by it before the exit step); if it is already noalloc the error stays 0. If error is 0 (including the already-noalloc case) it dirties the DTL leaves and the vdev config. Finally it returns spa_vdev_exit(spa, NULL, txg, error), so the value returned is the result of that call, which passes the error through and can itself return a different error (for example a failure of its transaction wait) even after the vdev was changed; the failure state is therefore not guaranteed unchanged.
note: Reviewers: original right (spa_vdev_exit's result is returned and the vdev may already have been changed); round 15 right (vdev_passivate's error, e.g. EINVAL, flows through 'error = vdev_passivate', 325-326). Callees not read.

name: get_special_prop
prose: Static int (zcp_get.c:224-453; the packet name zcp_get_ds_prop does not exist, the slice cut the head and also shows get_zap_prop) that looks up a dataset property by special-case code and pushes value and source onto the Lua stack. It allocates a ZAP_MAXVALUELEN string buffer and a setpoint buffer. For ZFS_PROP_CLONES it builds the clone list with get_clones_stat_impl: on success it pushes that list as a Lua table through zcp_nvlist_to_lua (VERIFY0) and then pushes nil as the source and returns 0; on failure it pushes nothing (so no table is left on the stack by this function), frees the list and buffer and returns the error. For the other properties it computes numval or strval in a big switch (ds accessors, objset/ZAP lookups for VERSION, VOLSIZE, VOLBLOCKSIZE, IVSET_GUID, RECEIVE_RESUME_TOKEN, encryption properties, etc.; unmatched properties are looked up in the dsl_dir with get_dsl_dir_prop). A non-zero error from that switch frees the buffer and returns the error with nothing pushed. Otherwise, depending on the property type, it pushes the number, the string, or, for index properties, the index string (zfs_prop_index_to_string; if that fails it frees the buffer and returns the error with nothing pushed), then frees the buffer, pushes the source with get_prop_src and returns 0. On success exactly two values are pushed (value then source) in the normal path and, for CLONES, the table and nil.
note: Real function is get_special_prop. Reviewer round 17 not supported for this source: on a get_clones_stat_impl error nothing is pushed (the Lua table is created only inside zcp_nvlist_to_lua after success, 247-251). The big switch cases were skimmed, not read in full.

name: zfs_set_prop_nvlist
prose: Applies a list of property settings to dataset dsname (zfs_ioctl.c:2766-2936; the slice cut the head). It returns the last error seen in rv (0 if none); errlist may be NULL, in which case errors are only reflected in the return value. For each pair it extracts the value (an nvlist wrapper must contain ZPROP_VALUE else EINVAL), validates the type against the property (for inherit the value must be a boolean; user properties must be strings and userquota ones uint64 arrays; others must match the property type, an index value must be a valid index else ZFS_ERR_BADPROP), then calls zfs_check_settable and, unless inheriting, zfs_prop_set_special. A result of -1 (not special) puts the pair into genericnvl; another non-zero result from zfs_prop_set_special in the first pass puts the pair into retrynvl, and that nvlist_add result overwrites err, so such a failure is not recorded in rv or errlist in that pass. Validation and settable errors are recorded immediately (added to errlist if given, and rv = err). After the first pass, if retrynvl is non-empty it loops again over retrynvl; failures there are recorded (errlist, rv) and are not queued again, while a retry that succeeds leaves rv and errlist untouched. If genericnvl is non-empty it calls dsl_props_set once; on failure it falls back to setting each property one by one (string, inherit or integer), recording each failure in errlist and rv. namespace-related properties set should_update_mount_cache, which triggers zfs_ioctl_update_mount_cache at the end. It frees both temporary nvlists and returns rv.
note: Reviewers: original right (errlist may be NULL); round 15 not supported: a pair that fails in the first pass is queued for retry without being recorded (2858-2865), so a successful retry does not leave a stale rv from that pair; rv can still be non-zero because of other pairs' errors. Callees not read.

name: zfs_replay_write2
prose: Replays a TX_WRITE2 log record by only extending the file size (zfs_replay.c:880-926, static int). It asserts the record length, byteswaps the record when asked, and returns the error of zfs_zget(lr_foid) if the znode cannot be obtained. At top it computes end = offset + length; if end is greater than zp->z_size it creates a transaction and sets zp->z_size = end BEFORE the transaction is assigned (so the size is changed in memory even if the assignment later fails), holds the SA, and assigns it with DMU_TX_WAIT. If the assign fails it releases the znode (zrele) and, for ERESTART, waits, aborts the tx and jumps back to top with zp already released (the retry then uses and releases zp a second time); for any other error it aborts the tx and returns the error (zp already released). On success it updates the SA size (result ignored), marks the log replay on the tx (zil_replaying) and commits. After the optional extension it releases the znode with zrele and returns error, which is 0 on the paths that reach the end.
note: Reviewers: original right (zfs_zget error returned; z_size is set before assign, not only on commit); round 15 right (the ERESTART path goes back to top after zrele(zp), 904-909).

name: zil_check_log_chain
prose: Dataset-iteration callback (zil.c:1264-1329) that checks that a dataset's intent-log chain can be walked. It ignores dp and asserts tx is NULL. It opens the objset with dmu_objset_from_ds; if that fails it logs a warning and returns 0 (the failure is handled here, so the objset is not required to be openable by the caller). It reads the log header's block pointer; if it is not a hole it takes SCL_STATE as reader only in this case (the lock is not taken when the log pointer is a hole), looks up the top-level vdev of the first DVA and, for a dead log vdev, computes validity with vdev_log_state_valid; an invalid result returns 0 without parsing. It also returns 0 if the pool has a checkpoint txg and the log header was never claimed (zh_claim_txg == 0). Then it calls zil_parse(zilog, zil_claim_log_block, zil_claim_log_record, tx, claim_txg, B_FALSE) with claim_txg = -1ULL when the header has already been claimed, else spa_min_claim_txg(), and returns 0 if the result is ECKSUM or ENOENT, otherwise the zil_parse error value (0 on success).
note: Reviewer round 15 right (the objset-open failure is handled, 1274-1279, and the SCL_STATE lock is taken only for a non-hole log pointer, 1284-1299). Callees not read.

name: zio_write_compress
prose: ZIO pipeline stage that compresses a write and sets up its block pointer (zio.c:1913-2131). It returns NULL (zio stopped) if zio_wait_for_children says it must wait for logical/gang children; returns zio unchanged (no compression, no transform, psize and compression untouched) if the zio is not an allocating write. It calls io_children_ready for parent blocks, and for a block already allocated in this txg (rewrite in syncing context) sets pass from the sync pass and turns compression off at or beyond zfs_sync_pass_dont_compress. If compression is on and the zio is not a raw-compress write, it computes psize: 0 for an all-zero buffer, lsize for ZIO_COMPRESS_EMPTY, else the result of zio_compress_data. psize 0 or psize >= lsize turns compression off (freeing the compressed abd when psize >= lsize); a result small enough for an embedded block (not encrypted, level 0, no fill, feature enabled) builds an embedded block pointer, frees the abd, sets the birth txg, sets the interlock pipeline and returns zio at once; otherwise the compressed size is rounded up to the allocation size, and if the rounded size is not smaller than lsize compression is turned off and psize = lsize (abd freed), else the buffer is zero-padded, psize = rounded and the compressed buffer is pushed as a transform. After a compression attempt it clears io_bp_override and restores io_bp_orig and the original pipeline. For raw-encrypted DNODE writes psize is 0 (and compression off) for an all-zero buffer, else lsize; for raw-compress non-encrypted writes it pads the data up to the rounded allocation size via a transform when that differs from psize; otherwise it asserts psize != 0. Then it either converts the zio to a rewrite (same txg, same psize, pass >= zfs_sync_pass_rewrite) or zeroes the bp and uses the write pipeline. If psize is 0 it sets a hole bp when the original had a birth and the hole-birth feature is active, and uses the interlock pipeline; otherwise it sets the bp's lsize, type, level, psize, compress, checksum, dedup and byteorder, and only if zp_dedup is set switches to the DDT write pipeline, and only if zp_nopwrite is set adds the NOP_WRITE stage. It returns zio.
note: Reviewers: original right (the non-allocating early return leaves psize and compression unchanged and pushes no transform, 1932-1933); round 15 right (the DDT-write and nopwrite stages depend on zp_dedup and zp_nopwrite, 2117-2128). Callees not read.

name: zio_vdev_io_done
prose: ZIO pipeline stage run after the vdev I/O completes (zio.c:4811-4857). It returns NULL (zio stopped) if zio_wait_for_children indicates it must wait for vdev children. Otherwise it asserts the zio type (read, write, flush or trim) and converts a non-zero io_delay start time into an elapsed time. If the zio's vdev exists, is a leaf and is not a dRAID spare: for non-flush zios it calls vdev_queue_io_done; with fault injection enabled and no error yet it may set io_error from device and label injection (any zio type); and only for an error on a zio that is not a FLUSH or TRIM it sets io_error to ENXIO when the vdev is not accessible, else it flags an unexpected error. It then calls the vdev ops' io_done (for a NULL vdev the mirror ops). If an unexpected error was flagged and vdev_remove_wanted is false it calls vdev_probe (result VERIFY0P-asserted to be NULL). It returns zio. So the ENXIO conversion and the probe apply only to read and write errors, not to flush or trim errors.
note: Reviewers: original right (the NULL return when waiting for children is omitted from the old text, 4817-4819); round 15 right (error conversion and the unexpected-error flag are skipped for FLUSH and TRIM, 4841-4842). Callees not read.

name: zvol_init_impl
prose: Initialises the zvol subsystem (zvol.c:2144-2227, returns int). It computes zvol_actual_threads: MAX(max_ncpus, 32) when zvol_threads is 0, else zvol_threads clamped to 1..1024. It picks the number of taskqs, MIN(max_ncpus, zvol_num_taskqs), or, when that is 0, 1 + max_ncpus/6 reduced while num_tqs squared exceeds the thread count; the threads per taskq are the rounded-up share. It sets zvol_taskqs.tqs_cnt, allocates the taskq pointer array (KM_SLEEP) and creates each taskq; if a taskq_create returns NULL it destroys the ones already created, frees the array and sets it to NULL and returns SET_ERROR(ENOMEM), which is the positive value ENOMEM (12), not -ENOMEM; zvol_taskqs.tqs_cnt keeps the attempted count and zvol_state_list, zvol_state_lock and zvol_htable have not been initialised at that point. On success it creates zvol_state_list, initialises zvol_state_lock, allocates and initialises the ZVOL_HT_SIZE hash heads of zvol_htable and returns 0. It reads module parameters and writes global state.
note: The earlier contract (result == 0 || result == -12) is dropped: the error value is positive ENOMEM (SET_ERROR(ENOMEM) at zvol.c:2213) and the function touches global state. Reviewers (mechanical rounds) only flagged the contract/prose mismatch.

name: HUF_compress_internal
prose: Static size_t (huf_compress.c:638-725) that Huffman-compresses src into dst, returning a compressed size, 0 (store uncompressed), 1 (single-symbol RLE) or a ZSTD error code. Checks in order: workspace not 4-byte aligned gives ERROR(GENERIC), workspace smaller than HUF_WORKSPACE_SIZE gives ERROR(workSpace_tooSmall); srcSize == 0 or dstSize == 0 returns 0; srcSize > HUF_BLOCKSIZE_MAX gives ERROR(srcSize_wrong); huffLog or maxSymbolValue above their maxima give tableLog_tooLarge / maxSymbolValue_tooLarge errors; zero maxSymbolValue and huffLog take defaults. If preferRepeat is set, repeat is non-NULL and *repeat is HUF_repeat_valid it immediately returns HUF_compressCTable_internal with the old table (this reuse path can return 0 or a size and is taken before any histogram, so it can precede the single-symbol check). Otherwise it counts symbols (a histogram error is returned), returns 1 after writing the single byte to ostart when one symbol makes up the whole input (this return does not update *repeat or oldHufTable), returns 0 if the data is judged not compressible (largest <= srcSize/128 + 4). If *repeat is HUF_repeat_check and the old table does not validate for the symbol range it sets *repeat = HUF_repeat_none. If preferRepeat and *repeat is not none it reuses the old table (compress-with-old-table return). Else it builds a new Huffman tree (errors from HUF_buildCTable_wksp or HUF_writeCTable are returned), writes the table header; with a usable old table it compares estimated sizes and may return the old-table compression, and it returns 0 if the header size plus 12 is not smaller than srcSize; otherwise it advances past the header, sets *repeat = HUF_repeat_none, saves the new table into oldHufTable if provided and returns HUF_compressCTable_internal with the new table.
note: Reviewers: original right (the single-symbol return does not update *repeat or oldHufTable, 674); round 15 right (the early reuse path with preferRepeat and HUF_repeat_valid comes first, 666-670, and can return 0). Callees not read.

name: ZSTD_compressBegin_usingCDict_advanced
prose: Starts a compression frame using a prepared dictionary (zstd_compress.c:3539-3571, returns size_t). It returns an error (dictionary_wrong via RETURN_ERROR_IF) if cdict is NULL. Otherwise it copies cctx->requestedParams and chooses cParams: the dictionary's own parameters (ZSTD_getCParamsFromCDict) when the attach preference is not ZSTD_dictForceLoad and (pledgedSrcSize is below the cutoff, or below dictContentSize times the multiplier, or unknown, or the dictionary level is 0); else parameters recomputed from the dictionary level, the pledged size and the dictionary size. Only when pledgedSrcSize is known does it raise windowLog to at least ceil(log2(min(pledgedSrcSize, 2^19))) (the source size is capped at 2^19, so the window log is raised by at most that much, not enough to cover larger sources; with an unknown size windowLog is not raised). It sets params.fParams = fParams and returns ZSTD_compressBegin_internal(cctx, NULL, 0, ZSTD_dct_auto, ZSTD_dtlm_fast, cdict, &params, pledgedSrcSize, ZSTDb_not_buffered), so the result is 0 or an error code from that call.
note: Reviewers: original right (the window log is raised only when the pledged size is known, 3559); round 15 right (the 2^19 cap, 3560). Callee not read.

name: ZSTD_compressStream_generic
prose: Static size_t (zstd_compress.c:3804-3943) running the streaming compression state machine. It asserts that the input and output buffers and the stream buffers are set and the positions are within their sizes. It loops while there is more work, switching on zcs->streamStage: zcss_init returns the error init_missing at once (so a stream that was not initialised is an error handled here, not a precondition); zcss_load either, for ZSTD_e_end with enough output capacity and an empty input buffer, compresses the whole remaining input directly (ZSTD_compressEnd, error forwarded), sets frameEnded and resets the session, or copies input into the internal buffer, ends the loop for ZSTD_e_continue when the buffer is not yet full or for ZSTD_e_flush when nothing new is buffered, else compresses one block (ZSTD_compressEnd for the last block, otherwise ZSTD_compressContinue; errors are forwarded), compressing straight into the caller's output when it has room, else into the internal output buffer and moving to zcss_flush; zcss_flush copies as much of the buffered output as fits, stops when output is full, and after a full flush either ends the frame (resetting the session) or returns to zcss_load. Errors (FORWARD_IF_ERROR, init_missing) are returned before input->pos and output->pos are updated. On normal exit it stores input->pos and output->pos, and returns 0 if zcs->frameEnded is set, else ZSTD_nextInputSizeHint(zcs).
note: Reviewers: original right (the init_missing error path exists); round 15 WRONG: the code returns 0 when frameEnded is set (zstd_compress.c:3941), the hint is returned only otherwise. Callees not read.

name: ZSTD_window_update
prose: MEM_STATIC U32 (zstd_compress_internal.h:938-972) that registers a new source segment in the match-finder window and returns whether it is contiguous with the previous one. If srcSize == 0 it returns 1 immediately and changes nothing (nextSrc is not updated). Otherwise it asserts window->base and dictBase are set. If src differs from window->nextSrc (a non-contiguous segment) it saves the old position as the extDict: lowLimit = old dictLimit, dictLimit = distance of nextSrc from base, dictBase = old base, base = ip - distance; if the extDict is smaller than HASH_READ_SIZE it sets lowLimit = dictLimit; and the return value becomes 0. It then sets window->nextSrc = ip + srcSize. If the new input overlaps the extDict (ends after dictBase + lowLimit and starts before dictBase + dictLimit) it RAISES lowLimit to min(dictLimit, the input's end index relative to dictBase), so lowLimit only increases there. It returns contiguous (1 unless the non-contiguous branch was taken).
note: Reviewers: original right (srcSize == 0 returns early without setting nextSrc, 944-945); round 15 right (the overlap code raises lowLimit to the smaller of dictLimit and the input end, 966-968).

name: ZSTD_selectEncodingType
prose: Chooses the symbol-compression mode for a sequence table (zstd_compress_sequences.c:143-221, returns symbolEncodingType_e: set_basic, set_rle, set_repeat or set_compressed) and updates *repeatMode. If mostFrequent == nbSeq (a single symbol) it sets *repeatMode = FSE_repeat_none and returns set_basic when defaults are allowed and nbSeq <= 2, else set_rle. For strategies below ZSTD_lazy with defaults allowed: it returns set_repeat if *repeatMode is FSE_repeat_valid and nbSeq < 1000 (leaving *repeatMode unchanged, so it stays valid), or set_basic (setting *repeatMode = none) when nbSeq is below the dynamic minimum or mostFrequent is below nbSeq >> (defaultNormLog-1); without defaults allowed this branch selects nothing and falls to set_compressed. For lazier strategies it computes the bit cost of the default table (if allowed), of the previous table (when *repeatMode is not none, which reads prevCTable, so prevCTable must be valid whenever *repeatMode is FSE_repeat_check or valid) and of a new compressed table, and returns set_basic (repeatMode = none) if the default is no more costly than both, else set_repeat (repeatMode unchanged) if the repeat cost is no more than the new table, else falls through. All paths that fall through set *repeatMode = FSE_repeat_check and return set_compressed. So after a set_repeat return *repeatMode can remain FSE_repeat_valid.
note: Reviewers: original right (set_repeat leaves *repeatMode unchanged, can remain valid, 176 and 214); round 15 right (prevCTable is read when *repeatMode != none, 193). Callees not read.

name: ZSTD_compressBlock_lazy_generic
prose: Static size_t (zstd_lazy.c:626-868) implementing the greedy/lazy/lazy2 match finder for one block; it appends sequences to seqStore and returns the number of trailing literal bytes (iend - anchor) that were not covered by a stored sequence. It reads the repeat offsets itself: offset_1 = rep[0], offset_2 = rep[1] (so the caller supplies rep[] as in/out, but does not have to prepare anything else beyond valid values). In ZSTD_noDict mode it zeroes any repeat offset that exceeds the current window (keeping one in savedOffset); in dictMatchState mode it asserts both repeat offsets are within dict plus prefix length. It chooses the search function by search method and dict mode and loops while ip < ilimit (iend - 8): at each position it first tries the repeat-offset match, then searchMax; with depth > 0 it runs the lazy search for a better match at ip + 1 (and ip + 2 for depth 2) and keeps the best; only the finally selected match for each iteration is stored with ZSTD_storeSeq (the other candidates found during the lazy search are discarded, not stored). After storing a match it also loops over immediate repeat-offset matches (stored with zero literals). When the loop ends it writes back rep[0] = offset_1 (or savedOffset if it was zero) and rep[1] = offset_2 (or savedOffset), and returns iend - anchor. It does not copy the final literals itself; the caller does.
note: Reviewers: original right (rep offsets are read from rep[] inside the function, 650); round 15 right (only the selected match is stored, ZSTD_storeSeq at 824, 842 and 857). Partly read: the body of the main loop (lines 691-862) was only scanned for the store, break and continue points, not read line by line.

name: ZSTD_decodingBufferSize_min
prose: Computes the minimum decoding ring-buffer size (zstd_decompress.c:1485-1494, size_t). blockSize = MIN(windowSize, ZSTD_BLOCKSIZE_MAX); neededRBSize = windowSize + blockSize + WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH * 2 computed in unsigned long long (WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH is 32 in zstd_internal.h:257, so the constant added is 64); neededSize = MIN(frameContentSize, neededRBSize). The result is neededSize converted to size_t; if that conversion changes the value (possible only where size_t is narrower than 64 bits) the function returns the error code frameParameter_windowTooLarge via RETURN_ERROR_IF, otherwise it returns minRBSize. There is no check against overflow of the unsigned long long addition itself, and no global state is read.
note: Reviewers: round 1 right (the wrap/size_t error path exists, 1491-1492); round 15 reviewer's claim that WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH * 2 equals 16 is not supported by zstd_internal.h:257 (value 32, so 64). The old formal contract is dropped (it omitted the error path).

name: ZSTD_estimateDStreamSize
prose: Estimates the memory needed by a streaming decompressor (zstd_decompress.c:1496-1502, size_t). With blockSize = MIN(windowSize, ZSTD_BLOCKSIZE_MAX), inBuffSize = blockSize and outBuffSize = ZSTD_decodingBufferSize_min(windowSize, ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN), it returns ZSTD_estimateDCtxSize() (= sizeof(ZSTD_DCtx), zstd_decompress.c:87) + inBuffSize + outBuffSize. The error return of ZSTD_decodingBufferSize_min is not checked, so an error code from it would be added into the sum like an ordinary size. The WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH * 2 term inside outBuffSize is 64 with WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH = 32.
note: Reviewers: round 1 right that the exact result is the sum including ZSTD_estimateDCtxSize(); round 15's 16-byte claim is not supported (WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH is 32 at zstd_internal.h:257).

name: load_tests
prose: Parses a crypto test vector file into a linked list (crypto_test.c:199-505; the packet name parse_test_file does not exist, the slice cut the head). It opens filepath (error message and failure if fopen fails), derives the base file name for messages, and reads lines with getline. A header section must give 'algorithm' (AES-GCM or AES-CCM) and 'tests' (a number); duplicates, unknown header keys, bad values or an incomplete header produce an error message and failure. Test records are key/value lines (id, comment, flags, result valid/invalid, and the hex fields iv, key, msg, ct, aad, tag); an unknown key, a duplicate key, an odd-length value or a non-hex character is an error. A blank line or end of file closes the test in progress: the test is committed to the list only if it has a non-zero id, all six hex fields and a result, otherwise it prints 'incomplete test' and fails, so completeness IS validated before committing. A read error (errno set) also fails. On any failure it frees the line buffer, closes the file and returns NULL (the tests parsed so far are not freed and *algp is not set). On success it frees the buffer, closes the file, prints 'no tests' if the list is empty, sets *algp = alg and returns the list head (which can be NULL when the file contains no tests).
note: Reviewer round 17 WRONG: an incomplete test is rejected before it is committed (crypto_test.c:241-252). Partly read: the hex-value decoding loop (lines 436-470) was only scanned for its error cases.

name: main
prose: Program entry (manipulate_user_buffer.c:245-335). It calls parse_options(argc, argv) itself (so options need not be parsed by the caller), then opens the target file with O_DIRECT plus O_WRONLY|O_CREAT for a write test or O_RDONLY otherwise; open failure prints a message and exit(2)s. It allocates a page-aligned buffer of blocksize bytes with posix_memalign (exit(2) on error). For a write test it fills the buffer with the repeated data pattern '0xdeadbeef' or, with randompattern, random bytes. It starts the buffer-manipulating thread and then the writer or reader thread; a pthread_create failure prints a message and exit(2)s (so thread creation success is not assumed, it is handled by exiting). It joins both threads, asserts args.entire_file_completed == 1 (an assert, so this check is absent when NDEBUG is defined), closes the file, frees the buffer and returns 0. All error exits use status 2.
note: Reviewer round 15 right (main calls parse_options and handles pthread_create failure, 257 and 296-322). Thread bodies not read.

name: main
prose: Program entry (xattrtest.c:669-715). It calls parse_args and returns its non-zero result immediately. If value_is_random is set it fills xattrbytes with get_random_bytes; the test 'rc < rndsz' compares an int with a size_t, so a negative rc would be converted to a large unsigned value and would not take the error branch; a non-negative short result prints an error and the function returns that rc, which can be 0 for a zero-length read, so this path can return 0 without having run any phase. Otherwise (value not random) it memsets xattrbytes to 'x'. It then runs the selected phases in order, each only when phase is ALL or that phase: create_files, setxattrs, getxattrs, and (unless keep_files is set) unlink_files; the first non-zero return of a phase is returned at once and later phases are not run. Returns 0 when all selected phases returned 0.
note: Reviewers: original, round 2 and round 15 right (the get_random_bytes short-read path returns rc, possibly 0, before any phase runs, xattrtest.c:680-685). The get_random_bytes return convention was not read.

name: pcg_output_xsh_rr_16_8
prose: Static inline pure function (pcg_variants.h:140-143) mapping a 16-bit PCG state to an 8-bit output ('xorshift high, random rotation'). It computes x = ((state >> 5) ^ state) >> 5 (done in int after promotion, so the intermediate is at most 16 bits wide), passes the low 8 bits of x as the value to pcg_rotr_8, and uses state >> 13 (a value 0..7) as the rotate count, returning the 8-bit result (value rotated right by that count; pcg_rotr_8 is (value >> rot) | (value << ((-rot) & 7)), or an equivalent rorb on clang x86). It reads only its argument, has no side effects and no failure result.
note: Earlier contract rounds failed (unbound pcg_rotr_8 / unbalanced brackets), so the contract is left empty. Checked against pcg_variants.h:56-66 and 140-143.

name: pcg_output_xsh_rr_32_16
prose: Static inline pure function (pcg_variants.h:145-148) mapping a 32-bit PCG state to a 16-bit output. It computes x = ((state >> 10) ^ state) >> 12, takes the low 16 bits of x as the value and uses state >> 28 (0..15) as the rotate count in pcg_rotr_16, returning the rotated 16-bit value (pcg_rotr_16 is (value >> rot) | (value << ((-rot) & 15)), or rorw on clang x86). No side effects, no failure result.
note: Contract left empty after failed earlier attempts (unbound pcg_rotr_16). Checked against pcg_variants.h:70-78 and 145-148.

name: pcg_output_xsh_rr_64_32
prose: Static inline pure function (pcg_variants.h:150-153) mapping a 64-bit PCG state to a 32-bit output. It computes x = ((state >> 18) ^ state) >> 27, takes the low 32 bits of x as the value and uses state >> 59 (0..31) as the rotate count in pcg_rotr_32, returning the rotated 32-bit value (pcg_rotr_32 is (value >> rot) | (value << ((-rot) & 31)), or rorl on clang x86). No side effects, no failure result.
note: Contract left empty after failed earlier attempts (unbound pcg_rotr_32). Checked against pcg_variants.h:80-88 and 150-153.

name: krping_wlat_test_server
prose: Static void (krping.c:1295-1327) server side of the write-latency test. It spins calling krping_cq_event_handler until cb->state reaches RDMA_READ_ADV, formats and posts the send of the start DMA address (ib_post_send; on a non-zero result it prints an error and returns). It then polls the completion queue with 'while ((ret = ib_poll_cq(cb->cq, 1, &wc) == 0));': because of operator precedence ret receives the boolean value of the comparison (ib_poll_cq(...) == 0), so the loop ends when ib_poll_cq returns any non-zero value, including a negative error, and then ret is 0; the following 'ret < 0' check can therefore never be true and a negative poll result is not reported, leaving wc unset when the loop was left by an error. If wc.status is non-zero it prints a send-completion error and returns. Otherwise it runs wlat_test(cb) and then waits interruptibly until cb->state == ERROR. It returns nothing.
note: Reviewers: original right (the poll error check is ineffective because ret is the boolean of the comparison); round 15 right (the loop also exits on a negative poll result and wc may be uninitialised; the 'waits for a completion' wording is not exact).

name: krping_bw_test_server
prose: Static void (krping.c:1329-1362) server side of the bandwidth test, with the same structure as the write-latency server: it calls krping_cq_event_handler until cb->state reaches RDMA_READ_ADV, posts the send of the start DMA address (print and return on a non-zero ib_post_send result), then polls with 'while ((ret = ib_poll_cq(cb->cq, 1, &wc) == 0));', which stores the boolean (poll == 0) in ret, so the loop is left by any non-zero poll result including a negative error and the later 'ret < 0' check can never fire, leaving wc unset in the error case. A non-zero wc.status prints a send-completion error and returns. Then, only if cb->duplex is set, it runs bw_test(cb); finally it waits interruptibly until cb->state == ERROR. It returns nothing.
note: Reviewers: original and round 15 right (same poll precedence bug at krping.c:1349).

name: vchiq_arm_force_suspend
prose: Forces the videocore to suspend (vchiq_arm.c:2132-2240, returns VCHIQ_STATUS_T). It returns VCHIQ_ERROR straight away (out label, only the trace log) if there is no arm_state. Otherwise it takes susp_res_lock for writing and calls block_resume; if that fails it jumps to unlock with its status, WITHOUT calling unblock_resume. If the state is already VC_SUSPEND_SUSPENDED it sets VCHIQ_SUCCESS and jumps to unlock (resume stays blocked). If the state is idle or lower it stops the suspend timer and: when videocore is not wanted it calls vchiq_arm_vcsuspend (its status, which may be a failure, is kept); else if autosuspend_override is below FORCE_SUSPEND_FAIL_MAX it returns success without suspending (letting videocore go idle); else it calls vchiq_arm_vcsuspend. In any other state (suspend in progress) it sets success. A non-success status from this step jumps to unblock_resume (so a vchiq_arm_vcsuspend failure ends with unblock_resume and that status). It then waits (dropping the lock) for vc_suspend_complete with a timeout: an interrupted wait gives VCHIQ_ERROR via unblock_resume; a timeout (once repeated if suspend is in progress) increments autosuspend_override, reports a timeout and returns VCHIQ_RETRY via unblock_resume. After the wait, if the state is not SUSPENDED it logs, resets the state to IDLE if it was an error state and returns VCHIQ_RETRY via unblock_resume. On success it jumps to unlock without unblock_resume, so resume remains blocked after a successful suspend. unblock_resume (when reached) runs under the lock, then the lock is released and the status returned.
note: Reviewers: original right (block_resume failure and a missing arm_state skip unblock_resume); round 15 right (a vchiq_arm_vcsuspend failure returns through unblock_resume, 2162-2181). Callees not read.

name: service_callback
prose: Callback delivering vchiq service events to a user instance (vchiq_arm.c:272-378, returns VCHIQ_STATUS_T). It maps the handle to the service (BUG_ON if none), reads the user_service and its instance, and returns VCHIQ_SUCCESS at once, doing nothing, if the instance is NULL or closing. Only when header is non-NULL and the service is a VCHI service does it queue the message: under msg_queue_spinlock, while the message queue is full it drops the lock, inserts an extra MESSAGE_AVAILABLE completion if none is pending (a failure of add_completion is returned), waits on remove_event (an interrupted wait returns VCHIQ_RETRY; if the instance started closing it returns VCHIQ_ERROR) and retakes the lock; it then stores header in the queue, advances msg_insert, may set skip_completion if a MESSAGE_AVAILABLE is already pending or a dequeue is waiting (clearing dequeue_pending), unlocks, ups insert_event and sets header = NULL. If skip_completion is set it returns VCHIQ_SUCCESS without a completion. Otherwise it returns add_completion(instance, reason, header, user_service, bulk_userdata): with the header pointer cleared if it was queued, or with the original header when the service is not VCHI or header was NULL (in that case the header is passed straight to add_completion and not queued in the message queue).
note: Reviewers: original right (the early VCHIQ_SUCCESS for a NULL or closing instance, 293-294); round 15 right (a non-VCHI service or NULL header is passed directly to add_completion without queueing, 304-376). add_completion not read.

name: vchiq_ioctl
prose: The slice is the VCHIQ_IOC_AWAIT_COMPLETION case (vchiq_arm.c:790-961) of the ioctl handler vchiq_ioctl (vchiq_arm.c:425-1156, returns int); there is no function named after the case. In this case: it returns -ENOTCONN if the instance is not connected. It copies the user args, takes completion_mutex and, while the completion queue is empty and the instance is not closing, drops the mutex and waits on insert_event; an interrupted wait sets ret = -EINTR and leaves the wait loop. If ret is still 0 it copies up to args.count completions to the user buffer: it stops at the first empty slot; for a completion with a message header it needs args.msgbufsize >= header size plus header struct (else it logs, WARNs, sets ret = -EMSGSIZE only if nothing was copied yet, and stops), needs a free user message buffer (msgbufcount), copies the buffer pointer from user space and the message into it (-EFAULT only if count is 0, otherwise it just stops), releases the message and replaces the header pointer with the user buffer; for a closed service whose close is not delivered separately it calls unlock_service; it copies the completion record to the user (an -EFAULT is recorded only if ret is still 0, then it stops) and advances completion_remove. It writes back the updated msgbufcount and count to the user args when they changed. If at least one completion was returned it ups remove_event; if ret is 0 and the instance is closing it sets ret = -ENOTCONN; a positive ret is reset to 0; the mutex is released. After the switch the common code of vchiq_ioctl converts a status of VCHIQ_ERROR/RETRY into -EIO/-EINTR when ret is 0 and returns ret.

name: vchiq_ioctl
prose: The slice is the VCHIQ_IOC_DEQUEUE_MESSAGE case (vchiq_arm.c:962-1020) of the ioctl handler vchiq_ioctl. It copies the user args and looks the service up with find_service_for_instance: -EINVAL if not found, or if the service is not a VCHI service (is_vchi == 0). Under msg_queue_spinlock, if the message queue is empty: a non-blocking call unlocks and returns -EWOULDBLOCK; a blocking call sets dequeue_pending and loops, dropping the lock and waiting on insert_event (interrupted: -EINTR) until a message arrives. It then takes the header at msg_remove, increments msg_remove, unlocks and ups remove_event. A NULL header gives -ENOTCONN; a header larger than args.bufsize logs, WARNs and gives -EMSGSIZE (the message stays dequeued); otherwise it copies the data to the user buffer when a buffer is given (a failed copy gives -EFAULT and the message is not released), stores the size in args, writes args back and releases the message. The case itself does not call unlock_service: the looked-up service is unlocked by the common code after the switch (vchiq_arm.c:1123-1124, 'if (service) unlock_service(service)'), which runs for every case that set the local service pointer, including the early -EINVAL breaks.
